selection.rule: Dependency-complete first 24 questions from the question-sheet selection order.

questions.question: In the story, what did the ruler give to each servant at the start?
questions.answer: He gave each one twenty-four gold coins.

questions.question: What does that show before they make choices?
questions.answer: It shows they began with the same chance.

questions.question: Did the ruler leave them with no way to travel?
questions.answer: No, he provided many travel options.

questions.question: What was one fast way of travel named in the story?
questions.answer: An airplane.

questions.question: How good was the result of his spending?
questions.answer: It brought a very great increase.

questions.question: How do we know he acted wisely?
questions.answer: He spent only a little and it brought a huge gain.

questions.question: What two good things might the servant receive from the master?
questions.answer: Forgiveness and a ride on a plane.

questions.question: What is the difference between the two servants in one short idea?
questions.answer: One plans wisely, and the other wastes foolishly.

questions.question: Which servant shows good judgment?
questions.answer: The one who thinks ahead and spends carefully.

questions.question: How many servants are in the story?
questions.answer: Two servants.

questions.question: What was the first servant like in his spending?
questions.answer: He was careful and wise.

questions.question: How much did the careless servant spend badly?
questions.answer: He wasted twenty-three gold coins.

questions.question: How did he lose nearly all his money?
questions.answer: He threw it away on bad entertainment and gambling.

questions.question: What kind of things did he choose instead of what he needed?
questions.answer: He chose useless fun and gambling.

questions.question: Why is wasting the last coin worse than it first seems?
questions.answer: Because losing that small coin means losing a much greater reward.

questions.question: What comes from the foolish servant’s search for fun?
questions.answer: Loss and trouble.

questions.question: What is said about the prescribed prayers at the beginning of the passage?
questions.answer: They are called the support of religion.

questions.question: What kind of place were they going to?
questions.answer: A rich royal farm.

questions.question: What did the first servant gain from a small expense?
questions.answer: He gained a huge increase.

questions.question: What was the second servant’s friend trying to protect him from?
questions.answer: From a long, hard, hungry trip.

questions.question: At the start, what did both servants have equally?
questions.answer: They both had the same amount of gold.

questions.question: Which servant used part of his money in a beneficial way?
questions.answer: The fortunate servant did.

questions.question: Which servant acted wisely with his money?
questions.answer: The fortunate servant.

questions.question: What does the friend believe about the master’s character?
questions.answer: He believes the master is kind and generous.
